title: Repeat whatever followed the current two-symbol context last time
summary: Predictions mix a fixed background distribution with a point mass on a remembered successor whenever the two most recent symbols have been seen together before. The memory behind this is a table keyed by ordered adjacent symbol pairs; each entry holds the symbol that came right after that pair at its latest occurrence.
core_idea: Store the latest follower of every two-symbol context and predict it again, blended with a fixed background distribution.

state.name: bg
state.meaning: Fixed background distribution over the V symbols, taken from training text.

state.name: F
state.type: table from symbol pairs to symbols
state.meaning: F[(a, b)] is the symbol that came right after the adjacent pair (a, b) when it last occurred, or empty.

update.name: latest follower
update.plain: F[(s_(t-2), s_(t-1))] = s_t, replacing any earlier entry for that pair

readout.name: blend
readout.plain: if the pair (s_(t-1), s_t) has an entry in the table F: P(c) = (1 - mu) bg(c) + mu * [c == F[(s_(t-1), s_t)]]; with no entry, P(c) = bg(c)

learning.description: Within a sequence only the table F changes. The background bg is the relative frequency of each symbol in training text (counting), and mu is picked by grid search on held-out text.
learning.few_shot_argument: A single occurrence of a two-symbol context with its follower already gives that follower probability at least mu when the context comes back.

complexity.constants_notes: Per symbol one table write, one table read and the V-entry output distribution; at most V^2 table entries.

prediction.statement: After a single occurrence of (a, b, c), the next occurrence of (a, b) gives P(c | a, b) >= mu = 0.75.

capabilities.task: associative recall of K pairs given as 'a b c' triples
capabilities.prediction: Exact whenever each probed pair occurs once before its probe, for any K up to V^2 distinct pairs.
Every continuation of a phrase seen once, whose two-symbol contexts are all distinct, gets probability at least mu.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: A context that occurred twice with different followers predicts the earlier follower.
After one occurrence of (a, b, c), the following occurrence of (a, b) gives P(c) below mu.

toy_example.description: Building the table on a short sequence over five symbols and blending for the final context.
toy_example.python:
import json
V = 5
bg = [0.3, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15, 0.1]
mu = 0.75
seq = [2, 4, 1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 1, 2, 4]
F = {}
for t in range(2, len(seq)):
    F[(seq[t - 2], seq[t - 1])] = seq[t]
ctx = (seq[-2], seq[-1])
P = [(1 - mu) * bg[c] + (mu if F.get(ctx) == c else 0.0) for c in range(V)]
print(json.dumps({"follower": F.get(ctx), "P": [round(v, 6) for v in P], "size": len(F)}))
